- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (negative) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward more aggressively.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overreacts with a prolonged upward bias; apply a lagged correction to dampen momentum.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to pivot; introduce a mean-reversion adjustment around the sentiment transition point.
- In low-sentiment or neutral periods, model tends to underperform; increase forecast volatility or add a small upward bias to capture hidden momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates the final 5–7 days; apply a small upward bias in the last 5–7 periods if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is mixed or oscillating, model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to prioritize recent sentiment direction.
